transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-03-21
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (HelioMesh Head of Partnerships), Carlos Ruiz (HelioMesh Cloud Ops), Priya Nair (HelioMesh Solutions Architect)

Optional summary: quick partner intro and technical discovery to scope integration and initial POC. Talked about VPC/private deployment, dedicated capacity, billing model, and security review cadence. Agreed to follow up with integration docs and schedule security deep-dive.

00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone thanks for carving out time, uh Jordan from Redwood here, I will run through a quick agenda, intro on both sides, then we can dig into architecture and what a partner flow might look like.
00:18 Maya Chen: Thanks Jordan, Maya on our side, excited to learn about Redwood, we run HelioMesh Cloud which is focused on GPU-first private tenants, mostly enterprise customers in media and healthcare.
00:29 Samir Patel: Hi all, Samir, I'm an SE at Redwood, I'll try to keep notes on integration points, especially around VPC networking and KMS.
00:36 Carlos Ruiz: Carlos, Cloud Ops, I might jump in on infra questions.
00:40 Priya Nair: Priya here, Solutions architect, I'll be driving the POC requirements and success criteria.
00:48 Jordan Lee: Cool, quick context, Redwood is a developer-first inference platform supporting hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private/VPC installs - the usual mix. We optimize for latency, predictable throughput, and cost controls like batching and KV caching.
01:05 Maya Chen: Awesome, interesting. A few quick things up front, our customers ask for tight colocation, SOC 2, and sometimes air-gapped options. How do you handle private deployments?
01:15 Samir Patel: For private, we offer a control plane that can be customer-managed, and an on-prem package for air-gapped. Integrations with KMS/HSM for key management and audit logs are standard. We do SSO/SAML and RBAC. There might be some nuance around network egress for telemetry.
01:30 Carlos Ruiz: When you say telemetry, do you send token-level metrics back to Redwood? We need to understand data flows and egress.
01:36 Samir Patel: Good question, by default hosted has telemetry, but for private we support an opt-out plus an offline metrics upload. We can also anonymize token-level cost breakdowns. We'll send the architect docs.
01:48 Maya Chen: That sounds promising. On pricing and partner economics, are you typically usage-based on hosted and commit-based for dedicated?
01:56 Jordan Lee: Exactly. Hosted is per-token/per-embedding; Dedicated is reserved monthly/annual capacity. For partners like you who operate cloud infra we often do partner revenue share or bring-your-own-infra options where Redwood software runs on partner hardware.
02:12 Priya Nair: For a POC we'd likely want to validate throughput with our A100s and your runtime, plus measure 95th percentile latency on a few prompt families.
02:21 Samir Patel: Perfect, we'll want sample workloads. Typical checklist: model family, sequence lengths, batchable vs low-latency calls, SLO targets, and desired qps. We can provide a benchmark harness and a spreadsheet for tracking.
02:34 Jordan Lee: I'll attach the benchmark spreadsheet and partner integration guide after the call (link: https://redwood.example/partner-guide - placeholder).
02:45 Carlos Ruiz: Are there special kernel/quantization considerations for the models we run? We usually run quantized models for cost.
02:52 Samir Patel: We support quantization-friendly execution paths and can recommend quantization profiles per workload. There are tradeoffs in quality vs cost; we have evals and prompt sets to measure regressions.
03:05 Maya Chen: On networking, we want to understand the VPC peering pattern. Does Redwood need inbound connectivity to our control plane?
03:12 Samir Patel: For private installs, control plane can be customer-hosted; if you prefer no inbound, we support outbound-only telemetry and pull-based updates. For Dedicated or hosted, we do region routing and it's outbound from Redwood to your compute if you host nodes.
03:30 Priya Nair: We also want to surface a security questionnaire to your team, especially around SOC 2, ISO, and audit logs.
03:37 Jordan Lee: We'll share the security pack and an initial SOC 2 attestation. We can do a deeper security review next week with our security engineer.
03:46 Maya Chen: Great. On latency, our customers often require sub-100ms token-latency or sub-200ms end-to-end for short prompts. Can you get that on A100 or H100?
03:57 Samir Patel: For short contexts we hit low latency on H100 and optimized kernels; A100 is competitive depending on batch sizing and sequence length. We can run a microbenchmark on both and show you delta.
04:12 Carlos Ruiz: How do you handle caching and KV cache? We rely on long chat sessions.
04:17 Samir Patel: Redwood has prefix and KV caching, automatic cache reuse for conversations, and a cache invalidation policy. Sometimes the docs spell it KV cash in auto transcripts, haha.
04:28 Jordan Lee: Also smart routing allows requests to be routed by policy, so sensitive accounts can stay on private capacity while burst goes to hosted.
04:36 Priya Nair: That routing split is important. We need to ensure compliance customers never leave our VPC.
04:42 Jordan Lee: Absolutely, we can pin model versions and routing policies per customer.
04:48 Maya Chen: Competitors like CloudScale pushed similar bring-your-own options, how is Redwood different?
04:55 Jordan Lee: Two big diffs: first, unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private so you don't have to re-architect; second, tooling for cost/perf tradeoffs like Intelligent batching suggestions, quantization profiles, and token-level cost breakdowns for debugging unit economics.
05:12 Carlos Ruiz: For the POC can we start with a small dedicated pool on your managed infra and then migrate to our nodes?
05:18 Jordan Lee: Yes, that's a typical path: start hosted/dedicated to validate behavior then migrate to private with a canary. We support rollouts and automatic fallback.
05:26 Priya Nair: About SLAs, what uptime and latency guarantees are offered for Dedicated?
05:31 Jordan Lee: We offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets on Dedicated; we'll share the SLA doc. Exceptions depend on region and commit.
05:38 Maya Chen: On integration side, what APIs do you expose for provisioning and autoscaling?
05:43 Samir Patel: We have an admin API and Terraform provider for provisioning routes, autoscaling policies, and capacity pools. We can give API keys scoped to partner accounts.
05:54 Carlos Ruiz: Any blocker around PCI/PHI? Some of our healthcare customers need PHI controls.
05:59 Samir Patel: For PHI it's usually private on-prem or VPC with customer-managed KMS and audit logs, plus contractual controls. We'll route you to our compliance team to discuss Business Associate Agreement stuff.
06:12 Maya Chen: Nice. For timeline, if we wanted an exploratory POC in April what's realistic?
06:18 Jordan Lee: If we get sample workloads by end of next week we can provision staging and run initial benchmarks in 2 weeks, then iterate. So April POC start is doable.
06:26 Priya Nair: Success criteria for us: throughput target met on A100 cluster, 95th perc latency under agreed SLOs, and documented ops runbook for failover.
06:36 Jordan Lee: Noted. We'll prepare a runbook and a benchmark report template.
06:42 Maya Chen: Any thoughts on billing integration? We prefer consolidated monthly invoicing and partner settlements.
06:48 Jordan Lee: We can support monthly invoicing and partner revenue share models; finance will follow up once we have scope.
06:55 Carlos Ruiz: Do you provide any demo code or SDKs for in-cluster inference?
07:01 Samir Patel: Yes SDKs for Python/Go and REST; also sample Helm charts if you want to run the runtime in your K8s.
07:09 Maya Chen: Cool. Also want to validate model onboarding - we run some custom LLMs trained by customers, will Redwood allow custom model imports and private model storage?
07:19 Samir Patel: Yes, private model onboarding is supported; we have model versioning and pinning, and storage options in S3-compatible buckets with encryption. We'll send the model onboarding checklist.
07:31 Jordan Lee: Quick note, I'll also share a partner integration doc and the benchmark sheet, see link (partner-guide and benchmark.xls in notes).
07:38 Priya Nair: Sounds good. Any regulatory notes for EU customers and data residency?
07:45 Samir Patel: We have region routing and data residency controls; for private deploys you can keep everything in-region.
07:51 Maya Chen: Great. Before we wrap, any open risks we should call out?
07:56 Carlos Ruiz: For me, network complexity and identity (SSO/KMS) are the two big ones.
08:02 Jordan Lee: We'll mitigate via security deep-dive and a joint runbook.
08:07 Maya Chen: Ok last thing, could you attach that preliminary SOW template and partner terms?
08:12 Jordan Lee: Yes will attach after call.
08:16 Jordan Lee: Recap and next steps: Jordan to share partner guide, SLA doc, SOC 2 pack, benchmark spreadsheet; Samir to prepare benchmark checklist and runbook; HelioMesh to share sample workloads and staging creds. Schedule security call for next week.
08:32 Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, excited to move forward.
08:36 Jordan Lee: Thanks all.

References and artifacts mentioned: partner integration guide (https://redwood.example/partner-guide - placeholder), benchmark spreadsheet (https://redwood.example/benchmark-sheet - placeholder), security pack (redwood.example/security-pack - placeholder), runbook template (link in follow-up).

Meeting ended 15:52 UTC
